How to play

The pages, mode by mode: which page to open, and what to press. The rules themselves are in the Rules, and each period's armies and battlefields in its book, such as The Medieval Wars, The Black-Powder Wars, The World Wars, Korea and Vietnam and The Late Wars.

Everything is kept in your browser, page by page, as you go. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you play online. To keep a game safe, or move it to another computer, use Save the game to a file on the campaign page (Saving).

Making the team (any mode)

  1. Open the team builder. Choose the Era, Where they come from and a Team, then press Roll the team. Reroll a man, or add one, as you like.
  2. Kit them out and buy from their purses if you want to.
  3. Press Send to the roller to fight man by man, or Send to the field map to fight with their followers as units.

On the roller the team arrives as an offer: press Add the team. Each man added becomes a named man at once (a team added again is the same men, not new ones): the travel map, the roller and the field map all know them, and they keep their wounds, purses and experience from page to page.

A fight at the table (the wound roller)

  1. Open the wound roller. Add fighters under Casualties (a name, then Add), or bring in the team (above). Give each his side, kit and weapon on his card.
  2. Press Roll initiative. The fighter whose turn it is shows Acting on his card.
  3. On the Battle map, click his token, then a hex, to move him. Click an enemy in reach to strike him; or mark the Attacker and Defender on their cards.
  4. Under Strike, choose the weapon (and an aim, if you like), then press Roll the hit. Where the blow lands and how badly is shown; press Apply hit to defender to put the wound on him. You may type your own d100 rolls in the boxes instead of letting the page roll.
  5. Wounds bleed and hurt each round. Give first aid from the wound on his card: Bind, Tourniquet or Cauterise.
  6. Press Next fighter when his turn is done; Next round starts the next round.
  7. When one side stands, open After the fight for deeds, loot and prisoners, and press To camp on each named man to send his wounds to camp with his force.

The GM's script (the pages play a side)

  1. On the roller, open Run the fight and tick it.
  2. For each side, choose who plays it: Player (a person, at the table or online), GM by hand, or GM's script. Choose how boldly the script fights, and the quality of men with no team-builder sheet.
  3. Press Step for one move of the script, or Play to my turn to let it play until a person's turn. Undo the script takes back its last step.

The script's men give first aid when no enemy is next to them: a man binds his own wound if it bleeds badly; a cautious side treats its worst-bleeding man it can reach, a steady side only its men who are down, a reckless side no one. A scripted man who is down with an enemy beside him asks for quarter and is taken prisoner; when a scripted side breaks, its men who are down or cornered surrender, and the rest run. Their cards say Taken or Ran.

On the field map the same idea is the Enemy commander: choose a commander for each side that should move by itself.

A fight online (the roller's Play online)

For a single fight with players on their own computers. In a campaign, use Players online on the campaign page instead: one link for the whole session.

  1. Set up the fight on the roller, with at least two sides.
  2. Open Play online and press Invite a player for his side. Send him the link (Copy the link).
  3. He opens it; his page gives him a reply code to send back. Paste it under his side and press Connect.
  4. He now sees his side's view of the fight and plays his side's fighters on their turns; you see everything. The script, or you, plays the other side.
  5. If he drops out, press Invite again and send the new link; he pastes it into Rejoin on his page (or opens it).

A battle (the field map)

  1. Open the field map. Add units under Add a unit, or send the team's followers from the team builder (Add them), or a battle from the travel map (Set up the battle).
  2. Place and order your units: select one under Units, then use the map and the Selected unit panel.
  3. Choose an Enemy commander for any side the page should move.
  4. Press Start the battle, then the same button again (it now moves the battle on) for each move. With a commander on both sides, Run plays on until you press Stop.
  5. Press End the battle to count the dead and carry the wounded; a battle from the travel map goes back with Back to the travel map.
  6. A battlefield laid out with its armies as drawn up shows Beat history: how the battle went, and how often the enemy commander wins each side playing against itself. When the battle ends by itself, each side the commander did not play is scored: against history, and against the commander's median run (the outcome first, then the enemy's men lost for each of yours). Your best result on each battlefield is kept in this browser, and the panel counts the battlefields where you have beaten the commander.

A campaign (the campaign page)

The campaign page is the GM's console over all the other pages. It shows the phase you are in, what to do in it, where things stand and the campaign's log, with the page for the step open in a frame below.

  1. Muster. Make the team in the frame (Making the team) and send it to the roller.
  2. Choose the map. Pick it from Map, beside the campaign's name.
  3. March. Press Done: on to march. On the roller, put each named man With his force on his card. Under Run the march, give each force its route or camp with Orders, then press Until something happens to move the clock on: forces march until one arrives, enemies meet, or a camp is finished, and the nights pass with their rest, food, sickness and events.
  4. Fight. When forces meet, Fights on offer lists the fight. Choose where to fight it (the roller, man by man, or the field map) and press Set up the fight; the console moves to the fight. Run it from the console's The fight panel (Run the fight, Step, Play to my turn), or on the page itself.
  5. Aftermath. First aid and After the fight on the roller; To camp for each named man's wounds. A field battle's result goes back with Take the battle's result into the travel map.
  6. Downtime. In the team builder: work, kit, and End of season for experience, rank and age. Then back to the march.

The console notices most things by itself (a fight sent, a man felled, a death, an outbreak, the end of a day or a season), moves the phase on, and writes them in the log. Add notes of your own to the log; tick GM only for ones the players should not see.

A campaign online (Players online)

  1. On the campaign page, under Players online, type the player's name, tick the named men he plays (one or more), and press Add a player. Only you decide which men are his: tick or untick them in his Plays: row at any time. (No men to tick? Send the team to the roller and press Add the team there.)
  2. His room appears with a code to say aloud (like WOLF-OAK-42) and a link. Send him either. He opens the link, or types the code on the campaign page; nothing comes back to you by hand. The log says when he joins.
  3. From then on his page shows his men, his force, his map (with the fog of war) and the campaign's news, and his fights on the console's roller come to him on the same link.
  4. He may propose orders for his force. Each proposal appears under Players online: press Accept (it is given as your own order) or Decline. Untick Players may propose orders to give all the orders yourself.
  5. If he drops out, or either page is reloaded, he is invited again and his page answers by itself.

To see what a side sees, choose As that side sees it from the view choice on the travel map, beside the map's scale.

No room server, or one that will not answer? Under Room server, press Copy and paste instead: you send him a link, and paste back the reply code his page gives him.

Playing as a player

  1. Open the link the GM sends you, or open the campaign page with a room code and type the code the GM gives you. (For a single fight the GM may send you a roller link instead: open it, and send him the reply code it shows.)
  2. Your men shows how each of your named men is, the force he is with, and his purse. Your force shows its orders, where it is, how many are fit, its fatigue, its route and its log.
  3. Your map shows your side's forces and, of the enemy, only what your side can see now (ringed red), or where it last saw them (faded). Hover a mark for more.
  4. To propose your force's orders, use Propose its orders under your force, or click a hex on your map (choose your force, and whether to march to the hex or go by way of it). The GM accepts or declines; your force's panel says which.
  5. When your man is in a fight, Your fight appears. On your turn: click a hex to move, click an enemy in reach to strike, choose your aim and roll (you may type your own dice), give first aid with Bind and the like, and press Next fighter when you are done.

Lost the connection? Leave the page open: your last screen stays, and with a room code it reconnects by itself when the GM's page invites you again. With a pasted link, ask the GM to press Invite again, and paste his new link into Rejoin.

Saving, and campaigns side by side

  • Save the game to a file (campaign page) writes every page's state and the campaign's log as one file: to back up, or to move to another computer. Load a saved game brings it back.
  • Campaigns in this browser keeps each campaign by itself as it moves on, with snapshots: Start another campaign, Switch to it, Roll back.
  • The lethality (Gritty, Standard, Heroic) and the units (US or metric) toggles at the top of the pages are shared by every page.

When something looks wrong

  • A page shows something old, or a new button is missing. Reload it (Ctrl+F5, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac) to get the newest version of the site.
  • A player cannot connect. Untick Public STUN server only when everyone is on one network; across the internet it is needed. A few strict networks (some workplaces, some mobile networks) will not connect at all: there is no relay yet.
  • Two tabs of the same page. They follow each other, but it is easiest to keep one of each page open, or to run everything from the campaign page.
